notes.note: Reading chosen: 'string equivalent' means the hex-digit text of the octets (per following sentences and example); character interpretation is oct2char.
Reading chosen: length counted in hex digits, i.e. result has two characters per octet (5 octets give 10 characters, consistent with the example).
Reading chosen: an octet above 7F causes an error; tested as runtime error (ttcn3verdict:error) with a variable argument. A tool may also reject it statically.
Informative NOTE; tested that oct2char returns non-graphical characters (codes 10 and 7), checked via char2int.
